Start with Fractions of quantities, Money & decisions, or Area & perimeter. Grade 4 selections in this tool focus on these topics. Let teachers attempt one question before revealing an answer. 3. Switch the SAME generated set to With bar-model support. Show how the diagram explains the quantities. title: Make It Count: teaching for understanding

text: Make It Count: teaching for understanding
Kaizen Maths  /  Make It Count
Bar modelling

Three quarters of a class is 18 pupils.
How many pupils are in the class?

What is the whole?
What does one equal part represent?

Our bar models explain the mathematics.
Pupils also practise without a supplied model.

About 2 minutes. Invite teachers to solve the class problem without support first. Three quarters is 18 pupils. Draw a whole as four equal parts: three parts together represent 18. One part is 18 ÷ 3 = 6. The whole is 4 × 6 = 24 pupils. Check that three quarters of 24 is 18. Ask what changes if a pupil divides 18 by 4: they have treated the known part as the whole. Discuss pupils' words as well as their numerical answer. In Make It Count, use bars to teach the structure, then give a fresh assessment-style problem without an added model to check independent understanding. Bar modelling is our chosen teaching scaffold. Do not present it as a mandated PEP response. Other mathematically valid strategies remain welcome. Grade-appropriate progression can include forward fractions before reverse fractions, then percentages, ratio and linked steps. Sources: assets/courses/bar-modelling-data.js and the teacher guidance in tools/pep-practice/index.html. Programme artwork remains the supplied Make It Count asset.
A proposed six-week programme
Kaizen Maths  /  Make It Count
Starting point
Select an NSC objective for Grade 4, 5 or 6.
Guided learning
Model fractions, percentages or ratio at the right level.
Classroom application
Teach a problem, then check an independent response.
Review and follow-up
Compare pupils’ explanations and plan the next lesson.
Session dates and school arrangements to agree together

About 2 minutes. Keep this a proposed six-week programme; agree actual dates with the school. Select an NSC objective and a grade before choosing activities. Cover fractions, percentages or ratio where appropriate, with reverse and linked problems as extensions. Start with a short teacher reflection and an independent pupil example. Work through modelled examples and teacher challenges, apply one strategy in class, and revisit a comparable fresh question independently. Discuss explanations and misconceptions rather than comparing only scores. Initial/final reflections support professional learning, not a causal claim of impact. Agree any research participation, consent and use of findings separately. Do not collect pupil names in course reflections. Ministry sources checked 19 November 2026: https://moey.gov.jm/curricula/ and https://moey.gov.jm/changes-to-administration-of-pep-to-accommodate-students-impacted-by-hurricane-melissa/ . The latter describes 2026-specific changes. Do not assume its test dates, item counts or component arrangements apply to the next examination sitting. Confirm the current Ministry/school bulletin before giving assessment advice.
Before we finish

Everyone can access the primary resources
One school contact for the programme
A Grade 4–6 objective and one classroom task
The next session and an agreed contact route
Which topic needs the most support in your class?

About 2 minutes. Confirm all teachers can access the primary tools and that the school coordinator knows how to raise access issues. Ask each teacher to name a Grade 4, 5 or 6 objective and one problem to use before the next session. Agree the next session and contact route. Ask: Which topic needs the most support in your class? Record the school's choice and use it to plan professional-development examples. Dates, school identity and contact details remain for the school to confirm. Close with questions. This deck is a primary-school onboarding and professional-learning guide, not an official PEP briefing or an assertion of Ministry endorsement.
